newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief condemns Tel Aviv cafe bombing.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief condemns Tel Aviv cafe bombing.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan, now visiting Africa, strongly condemned the bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe on Friday and said he hoped it would not be allowed to derail the Middle East peace process.
His statement, issued through a spokesman at U.N. headquarters, referred to an attack by a Palestinian suicide bomber that killed three people, including himself, and wounded more than 40 others.

"The secretary-general strongly condemns the bombing in Tel Aviv today causing death and injury to numerous civilians. He expresses condolences to bereaved families and to the government and people of Israel," the spokesman said.

"At the same time, the secretary-general wishes to reiterate his appeal to the parties not to allow odious acts of this nature to derail the peace process. He sincerely hopes that both parties will intensify their efforts to overcome existing obstacles to a speedy return to the peace process."
